name: Targeted Intron Retention
therapeuticGoalDescription: Force retention of a specific intron to generate a therapeutically beneficial transcript isoform — either a regulatory non-coding RNA, a transcript subject to nonsense-mediated decay (NMD), or a transcript encoding a micropeptide from the retained intron.
molecularDefect: Diseases where targeted NMD of a toxic transcript is therapeutic, or where a retained intron encodes a functional micropeptide or regulatory RNA.
diseaseMechanism: An ASO blocks a splice donor or splice acceptor site (or an intronic splicing enhancer) of a specific intron, preventing its removal during splicing. The retained intron either (a) introduces a premature termination codon triggering NMD, (b) encodes a functional micropeptide, or (c) creates a regulatory non-coding RNA that modulates gene expression.
suitableVariantTypes: Gain-of-function variants where NMD of the toxic transcript is therapeutic; diseases amenable to micropeptide-based therapy; cancers where intron-retained transcripts have tumor-suppressive function.
typicalDiseases: Experimental: gain-of-function disorders amenable to NMD (preclinical); cancer (intron-retained tumor suppressor transcripts); micropeptide-encoding introns (emerging biology, no clinical programs).
rnaTargetRegion: Splice donor site (5' end of intron); splice acceptor site (3' end of intron); intronic splicing enhancers; branch point sequence.
transcriptRequirement: Gene must have a functionally characterized intron where retention produces a therapeutic outcome (NMD, micropeptide, or regulatory RNA).
asoChemistry: RNase H-inactive steric-blocking ASOs (PMO, 2'-MOE, morpholino) to block splice site recognition without degrading the pre-mRNA.
designRules: Identify targetable introns via splice site prediction; validate intron retention consequences (NMD vs. micropeptide vs. regulatory RNA); design ASOs targeting splice donor or acceptor; validate by RT-PCR and RNA-seq.
secondaryStructureRequirement: Accessible splice site regions within pre-mRNA; intronic secondary structure may influence retention efficiency.
offTargetConsiderations: Potential unintended retention of introns in partially complementary transcripts; genome-wide splice site specificity analysis required.
advantages: Leverages natural NMD pathway for gene knockdown without transcript degradation by ASO; can generate micropeptides not encoded by canonical ORFs; reversible and tunable.
limitations: Requires detailed intron characterization; NMD efficiency varies by transcript and cell type; micropeptide biology is emerging; limited therapeutic validation.
clinicalTrialExamples: None identified. Preclinical and proof-of-concept studies only.

evidenceLevel.note: Strong mechanistic rationale from NMD and micropeptide biology, but no ASO-based therapeutic programs.
